text:
taylor: Quick sync — trying to lock down the audit event taxonomy for the RBAC + KMS changes. Need cross-team agreement on customer-visible names, redaction levels, and migration plan. Anyone got 10?
mina: SGTM. can we get a short delta from the current spec? main things I care about: actor/initiator fields, key_id leakage, and resource granularity.
jon: Product here — customers expect stable names. we should pick a clear convention. examples I hear: `key.rotate`, `kms.key_rotated`. prefer predictable dot-delimited like `domain.object.verb`.
sophia: infra note: runtime currently emits `kms.operation` with `{ type: "rotate" }` inside payload. that causes downstream mismatch w/ product expectations.
taylor: proposal: naming = `domain.object.action` (e.g., `kms.key.rotate`, `rbac.role.update`). use present-tense verb for action. also add a `visibility` enum so we can mark internal-only vs customer-visible.
mina: +1 on visibility. also we should add metadata fields: `redaction_level` (none|partial|full) and `sensitivity_tag` (pii|cfg|secret|none). linters should enforce masking rules for sensitive fields.
jon: for customer-facing events: DO NOT include raw `key_id`. surface `key_alias` or `key_thumbprint` only. customers asked for deterministic identifiers but not raw ARNs. docs must state masking rules.
sophia: note for BYOK/private: sometimes key IDs are customer-managed and needed for incident triage. suggestion: store full key_id encrypted at rest, but expose masked form in customer events (e.g. `k-***-8f2a`). add `key_id_hash` for deterministic joins.
taylor: example schema change I'm thinking of (high level):
```
{
  "name": "kms.key.rotate",
  "visibility": "customer",
  "redaction_level": "partial",
  "actor": { "id": "u-1234", "type": "user" },
  "resource": { "type": "key", "id": "k-***-8f2a", "key_id_hash": "sha256:..." }
}
```
mina: will add `actor.subject_type` and `actor.actor_origin` fields (to disambiguate service vs user vs automation). also will add linter rule to fail on any `key_id` in `resource.id` for customer-visible events.
sec-bot: CI alert: nightly audit-lint failed (2245) — rbac service emitted `rbac.role.updated` but current spec expects `rbac.role.update`.
taylor: thanks sec-bot. that's exactly the mismatch. Action items: (1) taylor -> PR naming convention doc and mapping table, (2) sophia -> runtime emission mapping + compatibility shim, (3) mina -> schema fields + linter rules, (4) jon -> update customer-facing docs and migration notes. target: EOD Friday for initial PRs.
mina: ack. I'll include a migration plan and a toggle `legacy_event_names: true` for 2 weeks to allow safe rollout. will add e2e test to block removal.
jon: I'll draft the customer note explaining the identifier masking and who sees what. Q: for compliance audits, can we provide a sealed admin artifact with full IDs on request?
sophia: yes — for enterprise/private we can generate a sealed export (encrypted with customer's KMS) and an access workflow. add it as `export.artifact` in the runbook.
taylor: perfect. sophia please link the branch when ready. sec-bot will run nightly checks after PR merge.
sophia: pushed branch `feature/kms-name-map` to staging, will open PR in ~2h. includes mapping table and fallback `rbac_compat` flag.
taylor: thanks all — if no blockers we can start rolling tests tomorrow. ping me here for any regressions. :thumbsup:
